questions.prompt: Which three things make up the fire triangle? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Fuel, oxygen and heat. Remove one and the fire goes out.

questions.prompt: Match each way of putting out a fire to the side of the fire triangle it removes.

pairs.left: Covering a pan with a lid

questions.explain: Water cools; lids and sand smother (cut off oxygen); turning off gas removes fuel.

questions.prompt: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its…
questions.explain: A substance must be heated to its ignition temperature before it can burn.

questions.prompt: Which is the HOTTEST zone of a candle flame?

feedback.1: The yellow zone is the brightest, not the hottest!

questions.explain: Complete combustion in the outermost zone makes it the hottest.

questions.prompt: Sort these into the correct type of combustion.

items.label: White phosphorus catching fire in air
A coal heap catching fire by itself

questions.explain: Rapid: quick with heat and light. Spontaneous: no spark needed. Explosion: sudden gas, heat, light and sound.
Complete combustion has plenty of oxygen: blue flame, CO₂ + water. Incomplete: soot and carbon monoxide.

questions.prompt: A paper cup filled with water is heated over a flame but does not burn. Why?
options: The water absorbs heat, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature
questions.explain: Heat is conducted into the water, keeping the paper too cool to ignite.

questions.prompt: Complete the word equation for the complete combustion of a fuel like wax.
questions.explain: Fuels containing carbon and hydrogen burn completely to form carbon dioxide and water.

questions.prompt: A candle under a large jar burns longer than one under a small jar. What is the best explanation?
options: The large jar contains more air, so more oxygen for combustion
The small jar reflects more light
questions.explain: The flame uses up oxygen; more air means more oxygen and a longer burn.

questions.prompt: Explain why burning coal in a closed room without ventilation is dangerous.
questions.modelAnswer: Without enough oxygen, the coal burns incompletely and produces carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas with no colour or smell. It builds up in the closed room and people can become ill or die from breathing it without noticing.
rubric: I mentioned not enough oxygen / incomplete combustion
I said it is poisonous and hard to detect (colourless, odourless)
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion + closed room = carbon monoxide danger.
